verdicts.title: On the Maximal Monotone Operators in Hadamard Spaces
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In this paper, some topics of monotone operator theory in the setting of Hadamard spaces are investigated. For a fixed element $p$ in a Hadamard space $X$, the notion of $p$-Fenchel conjugate is introduced and a type of the Fenchel-Young inequality is proved. verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In this paper, we study a family of lattice walks which are related to the Hadamard conjecture.  There is a bijection between paths of these walks which originate and terminate at the origin and equivalence classes of partial Hadamard matrices. verdicts.title: On the Asymptotic Existence of Hadamard Matrices
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: It is conjectured that Hadamard matrices exist for all orders $4t$ ($t>0$). verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns asymptotic existence of Hadamard matrices of order k2^{2+[ε log k]} via Paley constructions, not the minimum-distance defect of NW-design incidence matrices nor distinguisher advantage against NW pseudorandom generators.

verdicts.title: Brains and pseudorandom generators
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In a pioneering classic, Warren McCulloch and Walter Pitts proposed a model of the central nervous system; motivated by EEG recordings of normal brain activity, Chv\' atal and Goldsmith asked whether or not this model can be engineered to provide pseudorandom number generators. We supply evidence suggesting that the answer is negative.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns whether McCulloch-Pitts neural network models can serve as pseudorandom number generators, with no mention of Nisan-Wigderson designs, Hadamard/Reed-Muller code distance, or AND-of-parities distinguisher advantage. It shares only the broad term 'pseudorandom generators' and does not interact with the specific quantitative bound conjectured.

verdicts.title: Construction of Additive Reed-Muller Codes
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The well known Plotkin construction is, in the current paper, generalized and used to yield new families of Z2Z4-additive codes, whose length, dimension as well as minimum distance are studied. These new constructions enable us to obtain families of Z2Z4-additive codes such that, under the Gray map, the corresponding binary codes have the same parameters and properties as the usual binary linear Reed-Muller codes. Moreover, the first family is the usual binary linear Reed-Muller family.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes a Plotkin-style construction of Z2Z4-additive Reed-Muller codes and their parameters under the Gray map; it makes no claim about NW-PRG designs, distinguisher advantage, or linking minimum-distance defect to pseudorandomness bounds.

verdicts.title: Relative generalized Hamming weights of q-ary Reed-Muller codes
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Coset constructions of $q$-ary Reed-Muller codes can be used to store secrets on a distributed storage system in such a way that only parties with access to a large part of the system can obtain information while still allowing for local error-correction. In this paper we determine the relative generalized Hamming weights of these codes which can be translated into a detailed description of the information leakage [2, 24, 21, 11].
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract addresses relative generalized Hamming weights of q-ary Reed-Muller codes for secret-sharing/information-leakage on distributed storage, with no mention of Nisan-Wigderson generators, parity-AND distinguishers, or NW-design incidence matrices. It shares only the broad coding-theory vocabulary.
